subject: Organisational Behaviour
notes: OB core. No numerical questions apply; extra objective and case items included.

questions.text: Organisational behaviour is the study of human behaviour in
questions.subject: Organisational Behaviour
questions.explanation: OB studies how individuals and groups behave within organisations.

questions.text: OB draws knowledge from psychology sociology and
questions.subject: Organisational Behaviour
questions.explanation: OB is interdisciplinary drawing on psychology sociology anthropology and political science.

questions.text: The three levels of analysis in OB are individual group and
questions.subject: Organisational Behaviour
questions.explanation: OB analyses behaviour at the individual group and organisational levels.

questions.text: Organisational behaviour is a purely theoretical field with no practical application
questions.subject: Organisational Behaviour
questions.explanation: OB is applied and helps managers improve productivity satisfaction and effectiveness.

questions.text: State the disciplines that contribute to organisational behaviour
questions.subject: Organisational Behaviour
questions.correctAnswer: Psychology sociology social psychology anthropology and political science.
questions.explanation: Each discipline contributes insights at different levels of analysis.

questions.text: Explain the models of organisational behaviour
questions.subject: Organisational Behaviour
questions.correctAnswer: The main models are autocratic custodial supportive and collegial. They differ in the basis of control and in employee orientation moving from obedience to self direction.
questions.explanation: Describe each model and how employee orientation evolves across them.

questions.text: The process by which individuals organise and interpret sensory impressions is called
questions.subject: Organisational Behaviour
questions.explanation: Perception is how people select organise and interpret their sensory environment.

questions.text: Judging someone based on a single characteristic is called
questions.subject: Organisational Behaviour
questions.explanation: The halo effect lets one trait colour the overall impression of a person.

questions.text: A relatively stable set of characteristics that determines how a person thinks feels and behaves is called
questions.subject: Organisational Behaviour
questions.explanation: Personality is the stable pattern of traits that shapes behaviour.

questions.text: Attitudes have three components cognitive affective and behavioural
questions.subject: Organisational Behaviour
questions.explanation: Attitudes consist of belief feeling and intention to act.

questions.text: What are the components of an attitude
questions.subject: Organisational Behaviour
questions.correctAnswer: The cognitive component is the belief the affective component is the feeling and the behavioural component is the intention to act.
questions.explanation: These three components together make up an attitude.

questions.text: Explain the determinants of personality
questions.subject: Organisational Behaviour
questions.correctAnswer: Personality is shaped by heredity environment family social and situational factors. Both inherited traits and life experiences combine to form personality.
questions.explanation: Cover the heredity versus environment debate and situational influences.

questions.text: The theory that links effort to performance to reward is called
questions.subject: Organisational Behaviour
questions.explanation: Expectancy theory says motivation depends on expectancy instrumentality and valence.

questions.text: Learning through observing others and imitating their behaviour is called
questions.subject: Organisational Behaviour
questions.explanation: Social learning theory emphasises learning through observation and modelling.

questions.text: Job satisfaction is the positive feeling about a job resulting from evaluating its characteristics
questions.subject: Organisational Behaviour
questions.explanation: Job satisfaction is an affective response to the job and its characteristics.

questions.text: Distinguish between intrinsic and extrinsic motivation
questions.subject: Organisational Behaviour
questions.correctAnswer: Intrinsic motivation comes from the work itself such as interest and achievement. Extrinsic motivation comes from external rewards such as pay and promotion.
questions.explanation: The source of the drive internal or external distinguishes the two.

questions.text: Explain the reinforcement theory of learning
questions.subject: Organisational Behaviour
questions.correctAnswer: Reinforcement theory states that behaviour is a function of its consequences. Positive and negative reinforcement strengthen behaviour while punishment and extinction weaken it.
questions.explanation: Describe each type of consequence and its effect on behaviour.

questions.text: The stage of group development marked by conflict over roles is
questions.subject: Organisational Behaviour
questions.explanation: In the storming stage members experience conflict as they establish roles.

questions.text: The tendency of group members to suppress disagreement to maintain harmony is called
questions.subject: Organisational Behaviour
questions.explanation: Groupthink occurs when the desire for consensus overrides realistic appraisal of alternatives.

questions.text: A group is a set of people who interact to achieve individual rather than shared goals
questions.subject: Organisational Behaviour
questions.explanation: A group interacts to achieve shared goals; a team is a group with complementary skills and mutual accountability.

questions.text: List the stages of group development
questions.subject: Organisational Behaviour
questions.correctAnswer: Forming storming norming performing and adjourning.
questions.explanation: These are the five stages in Tuckmans model of group development.

questions.text: Explain the difference between a group and a team
questions.subject: Organisational Behaviour
questions.correctAnswer: A group has a common interest and individual accountability while a team has complementary skills shared goals and mutual accountability. Teams achieve synergy that groups may not.
questions.explanation: Cover goals skills accountability and the synergy of teams.

questions.text: The ability to influence others toward the achievement of goals is called
questions.subject: Organisational Behaviour
questions.explanation: Leadership is the process of influencing people to pursue goals willingly.

questions.text: Power that comes from a persons formal position in the hierarchy is called
questions.subject: Organisational Behaviour
questions.explanation: Legitimate power derives from the formal authority of a position.

questions.text: A leader who consults followers before deciding uses a democratic style
questions.subject: Organisational Behaviour
questions.explanation: Democratic leaders involve followers in decision making.

questions.text: List the bases of power identified by French and Raven
questions.subject: Organisational Behaviour
questions.correctAnswer: Legitimate reward coercive expert and referent power.
questions.explanation: These five bases explain the different sources of a leaders power.

questions.text: Explain the trait and behavioural approaches to leadership
questions.subject: Organisational Behaviour
questions.correctAnswer: The trait approach seeks qualities that distinguish leaders from non leaders. The behavioural approach studies what leaders do such as task orientation and people orientation rather than what they are.
questions.explanation: Contrast the two approaches and give examples of each.

questions.text: The shared beliefs values and norms that guide behaviour in an organisation form its
questions.subject: Organisational Behaviour
questions.explanation: Organisational culture is the shared values and assumptions of members.

questions.text: The physical or psychological response to demands that exceed a persons capacity is called
questions.subject: Organisational Behaviour
questions.explanation: Stress is the strain from demands that exceed available coping resources.

questions.text: Positive stress that motivates and improves performance is called eustress
questions.subject: Organisational Behaviour
questions.explanation: Eustress is beneficial stress that energises while distress is harmful.

questions.text: Define organisational culture
questions.subject: Organisational Behaviour
questions.correctAnswer: Organisational culture is the set of shared values beliefs and norms that members learn and pass on and that distinguish one organisation from another.
questions.explanation: It shapes how members behave and interact.

questions.text: Explain the sources and consequences of stress
questions.subject: Organisational Behaviour
questions.correctAnswer: Stress arises from organisational factors like role ambiguity work overload and poor relationships and personal factors. It can cause low performance absenteeism burnout and health problems.
questions.explanation: Cover organisational and personal sources and their consequences.

questions.text: Assertion: Employees with high job satisfaction tend to have lower turnover. Reason: Satisfied employees are more committed and less likely to leave
questions.subject: Organisational Behaviour
questions.topic: Learning motivation and job satisfaction (assertion reason)
options: Both assertion and reason are true and reason explains assertion
Both are true but reason does not explain assertion
Assertion is true but reason is false
Assertion is false but reason is true
questions.explanation: Satisfaction builds commitment which reduces the desire to leave.

questions.text: Match the concept to its meaning
questions.subject: Organisational Behaviour
options: Stereotyping - judging based on group membership
Halo effect - judging each trait independently
questions.explanation: Stereotyping judges a person by their group while the halo effect generalises one trait.

questions.text: The process of changing an organisation from its current state to a desired future state is called
questions.subject: Organisational Behaviour
questions.explanation: Organisational change moves the organisation toward a planned future state.

questions.text: Lewins three step model of change consists of unfreezing moving and
questions.subject: Organisational Behaviour
questions.explanation: Lewins model has unfreezing the change and refreezing stages.

questions.text: Resistance to change is always irrational and never justified
questions.subject: Organisational Behaviour
questions.explanation: Resistance may reflect genuine concerns about loss and can be a useful signal.

questions.text: Explain the reasons why employees resist change
questions.subject: Organisational Behaviour
questions.correctAnswer: Fear of the unknown habit loss of security and status and mistrust of management cause resistance to change.
questions.explanation: Understanding these reasons helps managers manage change.

questions.text: Read the case: A team misses deadlines because members rarely share information and avoid discussing disagreements to keep peace. Identify the group problem and suggest how to fix it
questions.subject: Organisational Behaviour
questions.correctAnswer: The team is suffering from groupthink which suppresses dissent. The leader should encourage open debate appoint a devils advocate and seek outside opinions before deciding.
questions.explanation: Diagnose groupthink and propose structural remedies to encourage dissent.

questions.text: Read the case: A talented employee has low motivation because she feels her effort does not affect rewards which she does not value. Use expectancy theory to diagnose and suggest a solution
questions.subject: Organisational Behaviour
questions.correctAnswer: Expectancy is low because effort does not clearly lead to performance or valued rewards. The manager should clarify the performance reward link and offer rewards the employee actually values.
questions.explanation: Apply expectancy instrumentality and valence to the described symptoms.

questions.text: A managers belief about whether employees are inherently lazy or self motivated is the basis of
questions.subject: Organisational Behaviour
questions.explanation: McGregors Theory X assumes people dislike work while Theory Y assumes they seek responsibility.

questions.text: The Ohio State studies identified two leader behaviours initiating structure and
questions.subject: Organisational Behaviour
questions.explanation: Initiating structure is task oriented while consideration is people oriented.

questions.text: The Big Five personality traits include openness conscientiousness extraversion agreeableness and neuroticism
questions.subject: Organisational Behaviour
questions.explanation: These five dimensions are the widely accepted Big Five model of personality.

questions.text: The extent to which a person identifies with a job and considers performance important is called
questions.subject: Organisational Behaviour
questions.explanation: Job involvement reflects psychological identification with the job.

questions.text: Explain the relationship between attitudes and behaviour
questions.subject: Organisational Behaviour
questions.correctAnswer: Attitudes influence behaviour through intentions but the link is moderated by situational constraints and the strength and specificity of the attitude.
questions.explanation: Specific strong attitudes predict behaviour better than general ones.

questions.text: Explain the importance of organisational behaviour for managers
questions.subject: Organisational Behaviour
questions.correctAnswer: OB helps managers understand predict and influence behaviour. It improves motivation teamwork leadership and the management of change and diversity leading to higher productivity and satisfaction.
questions.explanation: Link OB concepts to practical managerial outcomes.

questions.text: Describe the process of perception and the errors in it
questions.subject: Organisational Behaviour
questions.correctAnswer: Perception proceeds through selection organisation and interpretation of stimuli. Errors include stereotyping halo effect projection and selective perception which distort judgement.
questions.explanation: Trace the perceptual process then explain the common perceptual distortions.

questions.text: Job satisfaction is measured only through salary levels
questions.subject: Organisational Behaviour
questions.explanation: Satisfaction depends on many factors including the work itself supervision peers and growth.

questions.text: Explain the types of teams in an organisation
questions.subject: Organisational Behaviour
questions.correctAnswer: Teams include problem solving teams self managed teams cross functional teams and virtual teams. They differ in autonomy scope and how members coordinate.
questions.explanation: Describe each team type with its purpose and features.

questions.text: Explain the importance of emotional intelligence in the workplace
questions.subject: Organisational Behaviour
questions.correctAnswer: Emotional intelligence is the ability to recognise and manage ones own emotions and those of others. It improves leadership teamwork conflict resolution and customer relations.
questions.explanation: Cover the components of EI and their workplace benefits.
